title: Car camera
description: Live in-car video — the operator's browser connects straight to the vehicle's go2rtc (deploy/targets/<target>/go2rtc.yaml); no video bytes cross NATS or land in the database. The panel's nominal timescale datasource satisfies the dashboard contract; it queries nothing.

list.name: camera
list.label: Camera (go2rtc) base URL
list.description: http://<vehicle-host>:1984 — the vehicle SBC's go2rtc API listener. Default is the bench vehicle; override here at the track, no dashboard edit needed.

list.name: stream
list.label: Stream (go2rtc source)
list.description: car_h264 plays anywhere. car is the H.265 encode -- half the bitrate, but it needs a browser with platform HEVC decode (Windows/macOS; not Chromium on Linux).

list.name: mode
list.label: Player mode
list.description: mse is required for the H.265 `car` stream. webrtc is lower latency and fine for car_h264.

options.content:
This frame is the **vehicle's** go2rtc player, reached directly — telemetry does not pass through it and it does not pass through telemetry.

**Blank frame?** Check the two variables above first. `car` is the H.265 encode: it costs half the bitrate, but browsers will only take H.265 through a *platform* decoder — Windows and macOS have one, Chromium on Linux does not, and a Linux pit shows a black frame with no error. **`car_h264` is the default for that reason.** `mode` must stay `mse` for `car`: browsers will not take H.265 over WebRTC at all, and a default-mode player "succeeds" with a WebRTC session carrying **audio only**.

Still blank: check `${camera}/` loads at all (go2rtc's own UI). Only one stream can hold the camera at a time — close other viewers before switching between `car` and `car_h264`. Audio is muted by the browser until clicked.
